column1: # THE DECLARED CLAIMS OF THE PIPELINE — one row per cornerstone x boundary, WRITTEN BEFORE THE
# ARTIFACT IS BUILT.
# ==WHY A SECOND TABLE, WHEN `DECLARED.tsv` ALREADY EXISTS==
# `DECLARED.tsv` records WHAT AN ARTIFACT IS (`REAL`/`IDENT`/`TRIVIAL`/`LAW-JUSTIFIED`/
# `SINGLE-SIDE`/`BUDGET`) and is REGENERATED FROM THE OBSERVED STATE (`--declare`), which makes it a
# regression guard: it catches a cell whose kind changed.  It cannot catch a cell that was never
# meant to be `TRIVIAL` in the first place, because it learns the expectation from the emission.
# plan.md's fourth correction is the reason that matters: "Item 4's honest baseline is ~8 REAL cells,
# not 19.  Eleven of the twelve REAL `.egg` cells compare one program against
# `Reflect(tnodeOf(resT))` -- the executor's own output."  A table derived from what was emitted
# cannot report that, because the emission is exactly what is in question.  So THIS table is the
# CLAIM, written first, by hand, and 2A.1 is the task that fills it in; the audit then measures the
# artifacts against it (`scripts/audit_pipeline_markers.py`) and a cell that came out weaker than
# its declaration is a failure rather than a new declaration.
# ==THE SCHEMA==
# The column list is `Certified.ClaimsColumns` (src/main/scala/Certified.scala), declared in code so
# the emitter and the two readers cannot disagree about the order.  Tab-separated, `#` comments.
#   cornerstone    aunt | datalog-sn | gol | puzzle15 | temperature | nqueens | puzzle3-full
#                  (CornerstoneTypes.scala is the authoritative list -- seven, not six)
#   boundary       space | zipper | graph, i.e. which of the three stages this cell crosses:
#                    space   SPACE/TERM vs its optimisation (`SC.reduce`)
#                    zipper  the Scala `transpileZ` observation vs SPACE/TERM
#                    graph   `optimize(transpile(...))` vs SPACE
#   form           instance | agnostic.  `instance` is one ground input; `agnostic` quantifies the
#                  inputs and is the strictly stronger claim.  BOTH are declared per cell, because
#                  "the agnostic leg is TRIVIAL" is a fact about the emitter that a reader needs.
#   claim          one line, in words, of the equivalence this cell asserts.  It is prose on purpose:
#                  the machine-readable part is the other columns, and this is the part a reader
#                  checks the other columns AGAINST.
#   trusts         the `; TRUSTS:` list this cell is PERMITTED to carry, in `Certified.Trust`'s
#                  vocabulary: `T<n>` (docs/TRUSTED.md), `O<n><letter?>` (a registry's OPEN row),
#                  `law:<name>` (proofs/laws/REGISTRY.tsv), `outside:<construct>`, or `-` for
#                  nothing.  The emitted artifact's own `; TRUSTS:` header must be a SUBSET of this;
#                  a cell that trusts something its declaration does not permit is a failure.
#   artifact       repo-relative path of the emitted obligation.
#   expected-kind  REAL | LAW-JUSTIFIED | IDENT | TRIVIAL -- the `DECLARED.tsv` vocabulary.
#                  `SINGLE-SIDE` and `BUDGET` are deliberately ABSENT from what may be DECLARED:
#                  2A.2 deletes the single-side emission at its source and 2A.5 requires a BUDGET
#                  cell to be closed by decomposition rather than by budget, so declaring either
#                  would be declaring an outcome the plan forbids.  An artifact that comes out as one
#                  of them therefore fails against every possible declaration, which is the intent.
# ==STATE: FORMAT ONLY==
# 0.8 fixes the format; 2A.1 declares the rows.  There are deliberately NO data rows yet: a row
# invented here, before the independent-construction work of 2A.2, would be a guess at what the
# emitter will produce -- which is the very thing this table exists not to be.  The audit treats an
# EMPTY claims table as "no cell is declared yet" and says so, rather than as "every cell passes".
# cornerstone
